contexts.text: Where the carcase is, there are the eagles.
Under Corpse, see this reference.
Reasonings concerning goods and truths, that they only exist in so far as they are apprehended, and confirmations of evil and falsity by such reasonings, are eagles.

The reason the last state of the Church is compared to the eagles which are gathered together to a carcase or body, is that by eagles are signified the rational things of man, which, when predicated of things good, are rational truths, but when of things evil are rational falsities or reasonings... The birds which fly high, and have sharp sight, = rational things. Illustrated.

He led him about, He instructed him, He guarded him as the pupil of the eye, as an eagle stirreth up its nest, fluttereth over its young, spreadeth out its wings, taketh him, and carrieth him upon its wing (). It is instruction in the truths and goods of faith which is here described, and is compared to an eagle... An eagle, here, = that which is rational.
To ascend with a strong wing as eagles () = to grow in the understanding of truth, thus as to the Rational.

In , the eagle first mentioned = the Rational enlightened from the Divine; and the eagle mentioned in the second place = the Rational from proprium afterwards perverted by means of reasonings from sensuous and scientific things.
In , the first state of the Church is described by a lion which had eagle's wings, (which) = rational things from proprium.
The face of an eagle () circumspection, and thence Providence.
Hence it is evident, that an eagle, when predicated of man, = the Rational; and this because an eagle flies high, and from aloft takes a wide view of the things which are below.
Such was the signification of an eagle in the Ancient Church.
That in the opposite sense an eagle = rational things not true, thus falsities. Illustrated.
In these passages, eagles = the falsity which is induced by reasonings, which is induced from the fallacies of the senses and external appearances.
An eagle = the Rational.
The case is the same (as to sometimes having a good signification) with other rapacious beasts, as with leopards, and eagles.
I bore you upon the wings of eagles () = thus by means of truths they have been elevated to celestial light... An eagle = the Rational as to truth; for eagles fly on high. Explained.
In , is described the establishment of the Spiritual Church by the Lord; the eagle there = faith... The external of the Church is described by one eagle, and its internal by the other.
Good and thence truth in the internal form are signified by the face of a man and a flying eagle ().
The Spiritual Church is called an eagle (), from perception.

As they saw clearly the things below, I compared them to eagles... But they were indignant at this, supposing that I believed them to be eagles in respect to prey, and thus that they were evil; but I answered, that I did not liken them to eagles in respect to prey, but in respect to keenness of sight. I added, that those who are like eagles in respect to prey are evil; but that those who are like them only in respect to keenness of sight are good. SE 4673:4.
A great eagle with wings () = the interior truth of the Spiritual Church.

They who are in evil and at the same time in truths, may be compared to eagles which fly aloft, and which, when their wings are taken from them, fall down... Eagles also = men of prey, who possess intellectual sight; and wings = spiritual truths. It was said that they are such as have had no regard to God in their own life. To have regard to God in the life means to think that this or that evil is a sin against God; and therefore not to do it.

The fourth animal was like a flying eagle () = the Divine truth of the Word as to Knowledges and thence understanding. By eagles are signified various things; and by flying eagles are signified the Knowledges from which comes understanding; for, while they are flying, they Know and see. They also have sharp eyes, in order to see clearly, and the eyes = the understanding. To fly = to perceive and instruct; and, in the supreme sense, to look out for and provide. AR 320.
That eagles = such things. Illustrated.
In the opposite sense, eagles = the Knowledges of falsity, from which comes a perverted understanding. Illustrated.
There were given to the woman two wings of a great eagle () = the Divine circumspection for that Church... An eagle = intellectual sight, and thence thought.
The ensign of this heavenly Society was an eagle sitting upon its young at the top of a tree.
The courtiers wore mantles... in which were woven flowers around young eagles.
On the plate was engraved a young eagle, the nuptial ensign of this Society of Heaven.
At last we saw a grove of tall cedars, and on their branches some eagles...
By turns the understanding elevates itself, like an eagle... CL 1. CL 14. TCR 590.
There are some who at once perceive that truth is truth as soon as they hear it: in the Spiritual World these are represented by eagles.

They who confirm falsities of every kind, regarding truths as of no moment, and who discharge the offices of the priesthood only for the sake of gain, and to attain honour... may be likened to... leopards and eagles that with sharp eyes search for the richest prey.
To that faith, and the imputation thereof, the eagles have been gathered together (). Eagles, here, = the lynx-eyed leaders of the Church.
(Free nations compared to eagles.)
That Spirits fly to the spot like an eagle, as we read of the nations ().
An eagle = Divine intelligence.

The fourth animal was like a flying eagle = the appearance of the Divine protection and Providence in ultimates as to intelligence and as to clearsightedness on every side. An eagle = intelligence; here, the Divine intelligence which belongs to the Lord's protection and Providence. The reason an eagle = intelligence, is that intelligence is in the light of Heaven; and an eagle flies high in order to be there, and to look round on every side.

The reason an eagle = intelligence, is also because the birds of heaven, in a good sense, = intellectual and rational things; and an eagle pre-eminently so, because it not only flies high, but is also sharpsighted.
That an eagle = intelligence. Illustrated.

In , by the first eagle, is described the process of the regeneration of the natural or external man by means of scientifics and by means of Knowledges from the Word; and by the second eagle is described the process of the regeneration of the spiritual or internal man by means of truths from good; hence by the first eagle is signified the intelligence of the natural man; and by the second, the intelligence of the spiritual man. Explained.
That an eagle = intelligence, may also be evident from . To ascend with a wing as of an eagle = to ascend into the light of Heaven, thus into intelligence.
To be renewed like an eagle () = as to intelligence.
To bear as with wings of eagles = to bring into intelligence, because into Heaven and its light.

Their instruction in truths, guarding from falsities, and the opening of the interiors of their minds so that they may come into the light of Heaven, and thus into the understanding of truth and good, which is intelligence, is described by an eagle, its nest on high, its brooding over its young, and carrying them upon its wings (). AE 283:10.
By eagles () are signified those who are in truths, and who are in falsities; thus who are in true intelligence, and who are in false intelligence...
The falsities which are from man's own intelligence are also described by eagles in the Word. Illustrated. AE 410:4.
Eagles, here, () = man's own intelligence, which is reasoning from falsities.
An eagle, here, () = reasoning from falsities against truths.
They are compared to an eagle (), because an eagle, from its lofty flight. = the pride of man's own intelligence.

There were given to the woman two wings of a great eagle = the spiritual intelligence and circumspection which are given by the Lord to those who are of this Church... An eagle = intelligence and circumspection.
Moreover, the wings of the eagle, which were given to the woman = the understanding of truth; for all who are of that Church have the understanding enlightened...
(The eagle is a bird of an intermediate character, and appears in the World of Spirits.)

There then appeared eagles flying out of the desert... which swallowed the maggots, and licked up the slime like water... These eagles signified reasonings and confirmations (at the time of the abomination of desolation).
The spiritual man is like... an eagle as to the sight of the mind...
